words.word: En boca cerrada no entran moscas
words.reading: ehn BOH-kah seh-RRAH-dah noh EHN-trahn MOHS-kahs
words.meaning: Silence is golden / Loose lips sink ships (lit. 'Flies don't enter a closed mouth')
words.example: No le cuentes el secreto a nadie: en boca cerrada no entran moscas.
words.exampleMeaning: Don't tell the secret to anyone: silence is golden.

words.meaning: Put on a brave face (lit. 'To bad weather, a good face')
words.example: Sé que perdiste el trabajo, pero a mal tiempo, buena cara.
words.exampleMeaning: I know you lost your job, but put on a brave face.

words.word: No hay mal que por bien no venga
words.reading: noh ai mahl keh por byehn noh BEHN-gah
words.meaning: Every cloud has a silver lining (lit. 'There's no evil that doesn't bring some good')
words.example: Me cancelaron el vuelo, pero conocí a mi pareja en el aeropuerto. No hay mal que por bien no venga.
words.exampleMeaning: My flight got canceled, but I met my partner at the airport. Every cloud has a silver lining.

words.example: Por fin entregaste el informe; más vale tarde que nunca.
words.exampleMeaning: You finally turned in the report; better late than never.

words.word: A caballo regalado no le mires el diente
words.reading: ah kah-BAH-yoh rreh-gah-LAH-doh noh leh MEE-rehs ehl DYEHN-teh
words.meaning: Don't look a gift horse in the mouth
words.example: Ana se quejó del regalo. —¡A caballo regalado no le mires el diente!
words.exampleMeaning: Ana complained about the gift. —Don't look a gift horse in the mouth!

words.meaning: The early bird gets the worm (lit. 'God helps those who rise early')
words.example: Me levanto a las cinco para estudiar: quien madruga, Dios le ayuda.
words.exampleMeaning: I get up at five to study: the early bird gets the worm.

words.word: En casa de herrero, cuchillo de palo
words.reading: ehn KAH-sah deh eh-RREH-roh, koo-CHEE-yoh deh PAH-loh
words.meaning: The cobbler's children have no shoes (lit. 'In the blacksmith's house, a wooden knife')
words.example: Es dentista pero no lleva a sus hijos al dentista: en casa de herrero, cuchillo de palo.
words.exampleMeaning: He's a dentist but doesn't take his kids to one: the cobbler's children have no shoes.

words.word: Más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando
words.reading: mahs BAH-leh PAH-hah-roh ehn MAH-noh keh SYEHN-toh boh-LAHN-doh
words.meaning: A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush (lit. 'Better one bird in hand than a hundred flying')
words.example: Acepta la oferta segura; más vale pájaro en mano que ciento volando.
words.exampleMeaning: Take the safe offer; a bird in the hand is worth two in the bush.

words.word: A buen entendedor, pocas palabras bastan
words.reading: ah bwehn ehn-tehn-deh-DOR, POH-kahs pah-LAH-brahs BAHS-tahn
words.meaning: A word to the wise is enough (lit. 'For a good listener, few words suffice')
words.example: Ya te dije lo que pienso; a buen entendedor, pocas palabras bastan.
words.exampleMeaning: I've already told you what I think; a word to the wise is enough.

words.word: Dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres
words.reading: DEE-meh kohn kyehn AHN-dahs ee teh dee-REH kyehn EH-rehs
words.meaning: You are who you hang with (lit. 'Tell me who you walk with and I'll tell you who you are')
words.example: Cuida tus amistades: dime con quién andas y te diré quién eres.
words.exampleMeaning: Watch your friendships: you are who you hang with.

words.word: Camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente
words.reading: kah-mah-ROHN keh seh DWEHR-meh seh loh YEH-bah lah koh-RRYEHN-teh
words.meaning: You snooze, you lose (lit. 'The shrimp that sleeps gets carried away by the current') — Latin American
words.example: Aplica ya a la beca: camarón que se duerme se lo lleva la corriente.
words.exampleMeaning: Apply for the scholarship now: you snooze, you lose.

words.meaning: An ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure (lit. 'Better to prevent than to cure')
words.example: Vacúnate a tiempo: más vale prevenir que curar.
words.exampleMeaning: Get vaccinated on time: an ounce of prevention is worth a pound of cure.

words.word: El que mucho abarca poco aprieta
words.reading: ehl keh MOO-choh ah-BAR-kah POH-koh ah-PRYEH-tah
words.meaning: Don't bite off more than you can chew (lit. 'He who grasps much, squeezes little')
words.example: No te apuntes a tantos cursos; el que mucho abarca poco aprieta.
words.exampleMeaning: Don't sign up for so many courses; don't bite off more than you can chew.

words.word: No por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano
words.reading: noh por MOO-choh mah-droo-GAR ah-mah-NEH-seh mahs tehm-PRAH-noh
words.meaning: Things happen in their own time (lit. 'Just because you rise early doesn't mean dawn comes sooner')
words.example: Tranquilo, no acabarás antes por correr; no por mucho madrugar amanece más temprano.
words.exampleMeaning: Relax, you won't finish sooner by rushing; things happen in their own time.

words.word: Hablando del rey de Roma, por la puerta asoma
words.reading: ah-BLAHN-doh dehl rray deh RROH-mah, por lah PWEHR-tah ah-SOH-mah
words.meaning: Speak of the devil (lit. 'Speaking of the king of Rome, he appears at the door')
words.example: ¡Mira, ahí viene Luis! Hablando del rey de Roma, por la puerta asoma.
words.exampleMeaning: Look, here comes Luis! Speak of the devil.

words.word: Cría cuervos y te sacarán los ojos
words.reading: KREE-ah KWEHR-bohs ee teh sah-kah-RAHN lohs OH-hohs
words.meaning: No good deed goes unpunished (lit. 'Raise crows and they'll peck out your eyes')
words.example: Lo ayudé toda la vida y mira cómo me paga: cría cuervos y te sacarán los ojos.
words.exampleMeaning: I helped him his whole life and look how he repays me: no good deed goes unpunished.

words.word: Donde manda capitán no manda marinero
words.reading: DOHN-deh MAHN-dah kah-pee-TAHN noh MAHN-dah mah-ree-NEH-roh
words.meaning: Rank has its privileges / The boss is the boss (lit. 'Where the captain commands, the sailor doesn't')
words.example: Aquí decido yo; donde manda capitán no manda marinero.
words.exampleMeaning: I decide here; the boss is the boss.

options: Birds of a feather flock together
A bird in the hand is worth two in the bush
The early bird gets the worm
Kill two birds with one stone

items.question: What does 'En casa de herrero, cuchillo de palo' mean?
options: Don't judge a book by its cover
The cobbler's children have no shoes
Too many cooks spoil the broth
